HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.description:

of west to southwest winds. These stronger winds will continue
around Yap and Palau, lasting through Tuesday. Gusts up to gale
force, or 35 kt, can be expected at both Yap and Palau. Seas will
build in response to the increasing winds with hazardous conditions
expected at Yap, making inter-island travel dangerous, especially to
small craft.

as 97W, which sits just northwest of Yap near 11N137E. This
circulation, still showing a broad wind field, continues to become
better organized and is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone
Formation Alert by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center. This means that
the formation of a tropical depression is likely within 24 hours. As
97W lifts northward, winds and seas will gradually subside, first
across Palau, then across western Yap State.

Residents and mariners should keep up to date with the latest
forecasts for Yap and Palau by visiting weather.gov/gum or seeking
updated information from local Weather Service Offices and emergency
managers.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 12 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Weak south to southwesterly wind will result in minor sea level
rises. Expect rises of 1 to 3 feet above the normal high tide
line with each high tide cycle through Tuesday. Winds will be
around 10 to 20 mph through Monday, then weaken and shift
northerly on Tuesday.

The highest water levels, up to 3 feet above the high tide line,
are expected in Eastern Norton Sound while the Yukon Delta and
Nome Coast are expected to be around 1 to 2 feet.

Significant impacts are not expected but those with belongings on

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued July 12 at 1:46AM PDT until July 16 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Heat Advisory starting Sunday, temperatures of 85
to 98 expected. For the Extreme Heat Watch, dangerously hot
conditions with temperatures of 90 to 108 possible. Warmest
temperatures expected in the valleys.

* WHERE...Eastern San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles County Inland
Coast including Downtown Los Angeles, Los Angeles County San
Gabriel Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Susana Mountains, and
Western San Fernando Valley.

* WHEN...For the Heat Advisory, from 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PDT
Tuesday. For the Extreme Heat Watch, from Tuesday morning through
Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for dangerous heat illness for
anyone, especially for the very young, the very old, those without
air conditioning, and those active outdoors. There is a high risk
for heat illness for sensitive populations including the very
young, the very old, those without air conditioning, and those
active outdoors.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Monsoonal moisture will add to the discomfort
level from the heat starting on Sunday. continuing through the
week.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.
